name: Develocity
description: Develocity, authenticated by the host: the bottle talks to the server, and Claude Code (with the claude feature) to its MCP server, without ever holding the access key.

server.description: The Develocity servers, separated by commas, e.g. https://develocity.example.com,https://ge.example.com. Required: each is a host its access key is attached to, and one whose MCP server (/mcp) Claude Code gets.

keyFile.description: Where on the machine Gradle keeps Develocity access keys, as server=key lines (./gradlew provisionDevelocityAccessKey writes them). bottled reads each server's key from it each time the bottle starts; for a server it has no line for, `bottle auth login develocity` is used instead.

develocity.description: Develocity access key, from your user menu (My settings, Access keys); its user needs the 'Access build data via the API' permission. Read from the keyFile option's file first

bottle.context: Develocity (${server}) is authenticated by the host: send `Authorization: Bearer the-egress-proxy-holds-the-real-one` to a server and the host puts its real access key in its place. If Claude Code is installed, it has each server's MCP server (<server>/mcp), named develocity-<host> with dots as dashes (develocity-ge-example-com), set up that way.
